title: Layout
summary: Constraints, Row/Column/Expanded, Stack, overflow, LayoutBuilder, and slivers

lesson.heading: Constraints go down, sizes go up
lesson.body:
The golden rule: **constraints go down, sizes go up, the parent sets the position**. The parent passes the child a `BoxConstraints` (min/max width and height), the child picks a size within those limits, and the parent positions it.

**Tight** constraints (min == max) force an exact size: that's why a `Container(width: 100)` at the root of the app still fills the screen. **Loose** constraints (min 0) give the child freedom.

lesson.heading: Row, Column, and Expanded
lesson.body:
`Row` and `Column` are `Flex` widgets: they have a **main axis** and a **cross axis**, controlled by `mainAxisAlignment` and `crossAxisAlignment`. Non-flexible children receive **unbounded** constraints on the main axis and are measured first.

`Expanded` makes the child fill the remaining space (`FlexFit.tight`); `Flexible` lets it be smaller (`FlexFit.loose`). The `flex` parameter splits the space proportionally.

lesson.heading: Overflow errors
lesson.body:
Yellow-and-black stripes and `A RenderFlex overflowed by N pixels` mean the children exceed the available space: usually you fix it with `Expanded`/`Flexible` or by making the content scrollable.

The `Vertical viewport was given unbounded height` error comes from putting a `ListView` inside a `Column`: the Column gives infinite height and the list wants to expand forever. Fix: wrap the ListView in `Expanded`.

lesson.heading: Stack and LayoutBuilder
lesson.body:
`Stack` layers its children on top of each other; `Positioned` anchors them to the edges, and `alignment` places the non-positioned ones. `clipBehavior` decides whether anything that spills out gets clipped.

`LayoutBuilder` gives you the **parent's constraints**, ideal for making a single component responsive. `MediaQuery.sizeOf(context)`, on the other hand, gives the size of the whole screen and is preferable to `MediaQuery.of` because it rebuilds only when the size changes.

lesson.heading: Scrolling and slivers
lesson.body:
`ListView.builder` and `GridView.builder` build **only the visible items**: essential for long lists. `shrinkWrap: true`, by contrast, forces every child to be measured and defeats lazy building.

To combine collapsing headers, lists, and grids in **a single scroll view**, use `CustomScrollView` with slivers: `SliverAppBar`, `SliverList`, `SliverGrid`, `SliverToBoxAdapter`.

lesson.heading: In the interview
lesson.body:
Typical question: **"Why do I get 'unbounded height' with a ListView inside a Column?"** Explain the constraints rule: the Column passes unlimited height to non-flexible children, the ListView wants to take up the whole main axis, so the layout is undefined. Fix: `Expanded` (preferred) or a fixed height; `shrinkWrap` only for short lists.

Show that you know the "constraints go down, sizes go up, parent sets position" rule and the difference between tight and loose: it's the key to explaining almost any layout bug.

questions.prompt: What's the basic layout rule in Flutter?
options: The child chooses its position and size
The parent always forces the exact size
Constraints go down, sizes go up, the parent positions
Layout is computed at compile time
questions.explanation: The parent passes constraints, the child picks its own size within those limits, and the parent decides where to put it.
whyWrong: The child only picks its own size within the constraints it receives; the position is always decided by the parent.
The parent imposes constraints, not necessarily an exact size: with loose constraints the child can be smaller.
Layout happens at runtime, on every frame that needs it, because it depends on the screen and the content.

options: The ListView takes up the remaining space
The ListView is visible but doesn't scroll
questions.explanation: The Column gives unlimited height to non-flexible children and the ListView wants to expand across the whole main axis: you need `Expanded` around the ListView.
whyWrong: Taking up the remaining space requires `Expanded`: without it, the Column passes unlimited height and the ListView doesn't know how tall to be.
It's not a visible overflow: the ListView gets unbounded height and Flutter throws a layout error.
The ListView can't even lay out with infinite height, so it isn't shown at all: you get an error.

questions.prompt: How do you make a Row child take up all the remaining space?
questions.explanation: `Expanded` gives the child the remaining space on the main axis. An infinite width inside a Row causes a layout error instead.
whyWrong: Inside a Row the width is unbounded: `SizedBox.expand` tries to become infinite and causes a layout error.
`mainAxisSize` controls how much space the Row itself takes up, not how it's distributed among the children.
An infinite width in a Row, which passes unbounded constraints, throws an error instead of filling the space.

options: Expanded only works in a Column
Flexible forces the child to fill the space
questions.explanation: `Expanded` extends `Flexible` and forces `fit: FlexFit.tight`; with `Flexible` (loose) the child can be smaller than the space it's given.
whyWrong: Both work in any Flex: Row, Column, and Flex.
Flexible absolutely respects `flex`: it uses it to split the space, just like Expanded.
It's the other way around: Expanded (tight) forces the child to fill; Flexible (loose) lets it be smaller.

questions.explanation: The root receives tight constraints equal to the screen, so the Container's width and height are ignored. You need a `Center` or `Align` to loosen them.
whyWrong: The root receives tight constraints equal to the screen: the Container's width and height can't be honored.
Centering it would require a `Center`, which loosens the constraints; without one, the Container is forced to fill the screen.
MaterialApp isn't required: `runApp` accepts any widget, and a red Container doesn't need Material.

questions.prompt: When should you use `LayoutBuilder` instead of `MediaQuery`?
options: To adapt to the parent's constraints
questions.explanation: LayoutBuilder gives the space actually available to that widget, not the screen size: ideal for reusable components that live in different contexts.
whyWrong: MediaQuery gives the screen size, not the space actually available to the widget: they aren't interchangeable.
Density comes from `MediaQuery.devicePixelRatioOf`; LayoutBuilder provides constraints, not display information.
For the safe area you use `SafeArea` or `MediaQuery.paddingOf`; LayoutBuilder knows nothing about notches or system bars.

questions.prompt: A Row with long text shows "RenderFlex overflowed". What's the idiomatic fix?
options: Wrap the Text in Expanded or Flexible
Replace the Row with a Stack
questions.explanation: Inside a Flexible, the Text receives a finite width and can wrap or use an ellipsis instead of overflowing.
whyWrong: Shrinking the font only hides the problem for that text on that screen: with longer text, the overflow comes back.
A Stack would layer the children instead of placing them side by side: you'd change the layout instead of constraining the text's width.
`MainAxisSize.min` makes the Row shrink, but the Text still gets unbounded width and keeps overflowing.

questions.prompt: Why is `ListView(shrinkWrap: true)` with thousands of items a bad idea?
options: It has to lay out every child to measure itself
questions.explanation: To know its own height, a shrink-wrapped list has to measure all of its content, losing the benefits of lazy building.
whyWrong: A shrink-wrapped list still scrolls; the problem is that it measures every child and loses lazy building.
`shrinkWrap` isn't deprecated: it's handy for short lists and only expensive with many items.
`shrinkWrap` is about the extent along the scroll axis and doesn't cause horizontal overflow.

questions.prompt: You want a collapsing header + a list + a grid in a single scroll view. What do you use?
options: A Column with a ListView and a GridView
questions.explanation: Slivers share a single viewport and stay lazy. Nesting scrollable lists in a Column creates multiple scroll views or forces you into shrinkWrap.
whyWrong: A ListView and a GridView in a Column get unbounded height: an error, or else separate scroll views and costly shrinkWrap.
NestedScrollView is for when the header has to coordinate with separate inner scroll views; here a single viewport is enough.
Putting everything in a SingleChildScrollView builds every item up front, losing lazy building.

questions.prompt: In a Stack, how do you position a child 16 px from the bottom and right edges?
options: Align with bottomRight and a margin
questions.explanation: `Positioned` anchors the child to the Stack's edges. It must be a direct child of the Stack.
whyWrong: Padding alone doesn't move the child to the bottom right: by default a Stack aligns non-positioned children to the top left.
`Transform.translate` only shifts the painting and requires you to know the sizes: it doesn't anchor the child to the edges.
Align has no `margin` property: you'd need an extra Padding, whereas `Positioned` does it directly.
